items.summary: Disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide security clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Concrete evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication and access boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release provenance and approvals, dependency and supply-chain controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, complete TLS posture, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but this does not establish complete TLS coverage. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 35 pass, 14 fail, and 10 unknown, with open banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings. Retained worker and reviewer failures are containment signals, not evidence of compromise. Risk severity is high for public exposure and security-sensitive releases, medium for bounded growth. Exact decision: retain containment-only execution, keep the gated product private, continue existing read-only security evidence and failure repair-or-close work, and permit only reversible growth that preserves existing consent, disclosures, data handling, claims, and access boundaries. Do not create production work, requeue failures, add dependencies, change credentials or permissions, access private containers, deploy, collect duplicate telemetry, or conduct external outreach.

Retain the candidate plan's containment-only disposition and deferred backlog. No new security proposal, change request, data request, or production queue action is supported this cycle. Continue existing bounded read-only security evidence, legal/privacy evidence, measurement reconciliation, and failure repair-or-close work without treating missing telemetry as a pass or zero.
